analysis.evidence: וַיִּהְיוּ links the subject שְׁנֵיהֶם (“both of them,” the man and his wife) to the predicate adjective עֲרוּמִּים (“naked”), describing their condition.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed narrative וַ־
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: The suffix in שְׁנֵיהֶם refers to הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ, “the man and his wife.” The numeral indicates that עֲרוּמִּים, “naked,” applies to both.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine dual construct with a third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים, “both of them were naked,” the plural adjective describes the man and his wife together. The closing clause says they felt no shame about their nakedness.
analysis.morphology: Adjective, masculine plural absolute, used predicatively.

analysis.evidence: הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ (“the man and his wife”) identifies the pair referred to by שְׁנֵיהֶם (“both of them”). The definite article singles out the man already introduced in the narrative.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנֵיהֶם (“both of them”) refers to הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ (“the man and his wife”). The suffix וֹ refers to the man and identifies the woman as his wife.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ + feminine singular construct noun אִשְׁתּ־ + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 2:25 as an example under the existing Hebrew sense “not (of a fact)” in lo.
draft.definition: Before a verb, לֹא denies that its subject does or experiences what the verb expresses.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:25 uses וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ, “and they were not ashamed”, to describe the man and his wife.

analysis.evidence: In וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ, לֹא directly precedes the plural verb “they felt shame”. The narrator says that the man and his wife were both naked and that neither felt shame.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ־ “and” + indeclinable negative particle לֹא “not”.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנֵיהֶם identifies the man and his wife as the subject. עֲרוּמִּים describes them both as naked, and וְלֹא negates the marked verb, so the clause means “they felt no shame.”
analysis.morphology: Hithpolel imperfect, third person masculine plural
